title: Embedded resources
description: A tool result block that inlines a resource's contents together with its URI and MIME type.
question: Does an embedded resource keep its identity, or arrive as anonymous text?
notes: An embedded resource carries its own identity: a uri, a mime type, and contents. No adapter delivers it as a resource. One preserves the fields by stringifying them, one keeps the contents and discards the identity, two drop it. LangChain is unmeasured here: its audio conversion raises on the same result, so the call aborts before this block can be observed. Isolating it needs a fixture that returns one block at a time.

notes_by_num.1: CrewAI: the embedded resource is dropped from the result.
notes_by_num.2: OpenAI Agents: serialized into a text block holding the resource's JSON, so uri and mimeType survive as characters rather than as fields.
notes_by_num.3: Pydantic AI: reduced to a bare text block containing the resource's text. The uri and mimeType that identify it are gone.
notes_by_num.4: Mastra: all content blocks are dropped, embedded resources included.

verdict.headline: Delivered as a resource by none of the five.
verdict.detail: Once the uri is gone the agent cannot cite, re-read, or refer to what it was given.

usage_note: Not published. Candidate source: count of public MCP servers using this capability. Not estimated, so the panel stays empty until the corpus is scanned.
why: The URI and MIME type are what let a caller cite, cache or re-read the content. Stripping them to the inner text leaves the agent holding data it cannot attribute to a source.
